name: DRAC (Diabetic Retinopathy Analysis Challenge)
description: Computer-assisted automatic analysis of diabetic retinopathy (DR) is of great importance in reducing the risks of vision loss and even blindness. Ultra-wide optical coherence tomography angiography (UW-OCTA) is a non-invasive and safe imaging modality in DR diagnosis system, but there is a lack of publicly available benchmarks for model development and evaluation. To promote further research and scientific benchmarking for diabetic retinopathy analysis using UW-OCTA images, we organized a challenge named "DRAC - Diabetic Retinopathy Analysis Challenge" in conjunction with the 25th International Conference on Medical Image Computing and Computer Assisted Intervention (MICCAI 2022). The challenge consists of three tasks: segmentation of DR lesions, image quality assessment and DR grading. The scientific community responded positively to the challenge, with 11, 12, and 13 teams from geographically diverse institutes submitting different solutions in these three tasks, respectively. This paper presents a summary and analysis of the top-performing solutions and results for each task of the challenge. The obtained results from top algorithms indicate the importance of data augmentation, model architecture and ensemble of networks in improving the performance of deep learning models. These findings have the potential to enable new developments in diabetic retinopathy analysis. The challenge remains open for post-challenge registrations and submissions for benchmarking future methodology developments.
evaluation_method: Dice / F1 for segmentation; accuracy / AUROC for image quality assessment and DR grading
general_score_metric: Dice coefficient (F1) for segmentation (primary); accuracy / AUROC for the other tasks
typical_sota_score: Segmentation (Dice/F1): ~50–85%; Image quality assessment & DR grading (accuracy/AUROC): ~70–90%
reputation: Organized as a MICCAI 2022 challenge and used by the medical imaging community for UW‑OCTA diabetic retinopathy research; moderate niche adoption.
notes: Medical-imaging benchmark (non-LLM); multi-task evaluation with different primary metrics per task; limited to UW‑OCTA modality so dataset size and domain shift limit generalization; labeling variability across graders; challenge remains open for post-challenge submissions.
